newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Accused Peruvian drug lord held in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Accused Peruvian drug lord held in Colombia.

text.p: An accused Peruvian drug kingpin, alleged by authorities to be a top supplier of cocaine base to Colombian traffickers, was arrested on Thursday in Bogota, police said.

The National Police said in a statement that Enrique Cardenas Guzman, known in Peru as "Mosquito" or "Little Fly", was wanted on two outstanding drug charges in Peru where is the target of an extradition request from Interpol officials.
Cardenas Guzman was arrested by secret police agents after being found with a woman in a luxury apartment in north Bogota, the statement said.
It said he had taken over as head of a powerful drug gang after his father, nicknamed "Crazy Fly" and the group's previous boss, died in a Lima prison riot.

Three-quarters of the world's cocaine is produced in Colombia. U.S. drug agents say most of it is produced in clandestine drug laboratories that convert cocaine base smuggled into the country from Peru into pure cocaine.
